conclusion: Existing APIs can measure default C4 versus existing reflex behavior on exact extracted static coordinates, with a small measurement-only explicit-cell adapter. They cannot currently reproduce a complete evolved adult state or implement a matched three-arm BH3 handoff.
available: Saved K traces preserve exact cell sites, birth/death times and full terminal phenotypes.
The controller path consumes an explicit cell list, so an adapter can preserve an irregular fixed geometry and ordering.
Existing role_body can apply retained reflex knobs to supplied sense/act sites; inert hidden cells can retain their living cost.
The information_share readout already validates common seeds, full world/window and footprint protocol identifiers and computes the paired ratio.
limitations: The built-in Footprint.hidden interface creates uniform layers above all act sites; none of the24 observed t800/final K snapshots matches it exactly.
The12 final trace bodies have118–212 distinct full phenotypes; the fixed program has only five phenotype rows.

Explicit initialization has coordinates and program row, not per-cell gene state, membrane/refractory state, learned weights, chemistry, clocks or original identities. All initial cells are born at t0.
C4 executes only in program mode; the existing freeze clone preserves adult state but cannot transfer control to C4.
A final body rebuilt at t0 changes development costs, sensing history and initial state. Ordinary growing-life evolved F cannot honestly be combined with that static C4/reflex gap as exact BH3.
honest_estimand: C4 minus an unchanged retained reflex on a specified frozen snapshot geometry, both starting afresh under an identical world/window. This is conditional geometry headroom, not the fraction of the information gap used by the growing organism.
recommendation: Prioritize the already proposed ordinary16-generation continuations from both fixed D endpoints for a direct adaptation result. Keep static geometry headroom as a separately labeled diagnostic. Exact BH3 needs a prospectively specified common development/state-handoff protocol and implementation review; metadata alone cannot establish matching.
